long_biography.plain_text:
Three Seas Maritime formalised work that Matthew Csidei had already been conducting independently. In 2018 he transferred that Monaco business into a new partnership and became one of its managers. The company began with purchase assistance, repair and renovation services, giving private clients a single point of coordination for complex marine projects.

A later expansion added sales, charter, administrative and technical management, design, maintenance supervision and materials sourcing. Related property assignments entered the remit as an ancillary service to maritime clients. The structure placed Csidei on both the ownership and operating sides of the venture, with responsibility rooted in practical project delivery.

review.notes: Owner-tag consolidation research context: [1] Construction project management: Csidei was the sole director and secretary of Manoc Developments when it was engaged to oversee a major residential development for James Packer, making construction-project coordination a durable part of his documented professional record. [2] Executive equity ownership: At Three Seas Maritime's formation, Csidei simultaneously held an ownership interest as an associate and an operating office as manager. [3] Integrated marine services: Three Seas Maritime combines purchase assistance, repair and renovation with sales, charter, agency, administrative and technical management, design, maintenance supervision and materials sourcing on one marine-services platform. [4] Manager co-ownership: Three Seas Maritime was formed as a partnership in which Csidei was documented as both an associate and a manager, placing him on the ownership and management sides of the business. [5] Manoc Developments: Csidei was sole director and secretary of Manoc Developments when the company oversaw a major residential project for James Packer, making it a material earlier business association rather than a tangential employer. [6] Marine agency services: The official expansion of Three Seas Maritime expressly added marine-agency services, a broader private-client service concept than the catalogue's port-oriented Ship agency tag. [7] Marine project management: Csidei's company coordinates purchase, repair, renovation, design, maintenance and technical-management work for complex marine projects, a distinct professional-services cohort not captured by generic ship management. [8] Marine purchase advisory: Purchase assistance and advice formed part of Three Seas Maritime's original objects, supporting a durable buyer-side marine advisory grouping without assuming yacht brokerage or commercial shipbroking. [9] Marine repair and renovation services: Repair and renovation were core objects of Csidei's predecessor activity and Three Seas Maritime at incorporation, but the dossier does not establish a shipyard or commercial-ship focus. [10] Marine sales and charter services: Three Seas Maritime's expanded objects expressly include marine sales and charter services, a service segment broader than the catalogue's yacht-only and commercial-ship brokerage concepts. [11] Marine technical management: Three Seas Maritime's official objects include administrative and technical management, design and maintenance supervision for marine projects, while the dossier does not establish the fleet scope implied by Technical ship management. [12] Maritime entrepreneur: Csidei contributed an existing independently operated Monaco marine business to the newly incorporated Three Seas Maritime and became its founding manager. [13] Property-to-maritime entrepreneurship transition: Csidei moved from leading property-project work through Manoc Developments to contributing an independently operated Monaco marine business into Three Seas Maritime and managing the new partnership. [14] Three Seas Maritime: The Monaco company is Csidei's defining independent venture: he contributed its predecessor business, became an associate-manager and helped build a broad marine-services platform.
